answer: In an agent marketplace trading everything from shale samples to pearl jewelry, each identity must lock a fixed bond for 90 days before it can bid, with one active bid allowed per bond. Creating more names therefore cannot produce a free spiral of bidding power: an attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous bids must fund 1,000 bonds and forgo access to that capital for the full lock period, even if the identities are never linked.
